title: Work scheme interaction
question: How should /workscheme feel more interactive while staying inside The Parchment Atelier system?

options.label: Scroll spine
options.thesis: Sticky stage index tracks scroll; the active step lights as you move through the sequence.
options.viewport: Clean headline + short support; then a vertical sequence with a sticky progress rail.
options.case: Best for a long factual process: motion explains place in the journey without hiding content.
options.risk: Needs careful sticky/mobile behavior so the rail does not fight Lenis.

options.label: Atelier panel
options.thesis: Left index of all stages; right panel shows one focused step at a time with prev/next.
options.viewport: Split composition: numbered index beside a large stage title and body.
options.case: Most interactive; turns the page into a guided walkthrough.
options.risk: Can feel Operate-heavy for a Persuade marketing route; mobile needs a stacked fallback.

options.label: Expand stages
options.thesis: Compact stage list; click/tap a row to expand body copy with a quiet height transition.
options.viewport: Dense editorial list of titles; one open stage at a time.
options.case: Clean and scannable; interaction is disclosure, not spectacle.
options.risk: Hides process detail until click; weaker for first-time readers who only skim.

options.label: Editorial clean
options.thesis: Keep the open list, but refine hierarchy, copy, and CTA to match About/dark-band patterns—no new interaction model.
options.viewport: Stronger headline measure, clearer stage rhythm, dark CTA band.
options.case: Safest polish if interaction is secondary to clarity.
options.risk: May feel under-interactive vs the request.
options.kept: Copy clarity and dark-band CTA still apply to any pick.
